subject: Extended Price Preservation Petition – multi-year price lock + renewal protection
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudbridge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudbridge.com
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal — ask on multi-year pricing protection

Neha,

Thanks for the proposal. We like the model and performance, but procurement is pushing for a three-year price preservation clause and a cap on any annual uplift at 3% to secure budgeting across our product line.

Can Redwood commit to a 36-month price lock with an uplift cap and a renewal protection clause that guarantees no material change to core per-unit pricing without 180 days' notice? If you can get exec signoff on that, we can expedite the procurement review.

Attached our redline (see Contract_V1 markups).

Elena
CloudBridge — Head of Procurement
Attachment: CloudBridge_Contract_V1.pdf (redline)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 09:50:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Redwood proposal — ask on multi-year pricing protection

Team — forwarding CloudBridge's ask. Key asks: 3yr price lock, max 3% annual uplift, 180-day notice on material pricing changes. They say expedited procurement if we sign off.

Ben: can Deal Desk support 3% uplift cap operationally? Marissa: is there an acceptable renewal protection language we can offer that doesn't expose us to open-ended obligations? Priyom: if we do this, what’s the estimated ARR impact and what guardrails should we add (e.g., CPI pass-through, change in compute cost trigger)?

My suggested quick path: 1) exec exception for term + uplift cap, 2) add escalation clause for major underlying cloud/hardware cost increases that allows limited pass-through, and 3) require annual review with customer success to monitor usage.

I'll prep a short exec note if you confirm we can price-protect. Need a response by 2pm PT to move procurement.

Thanks — Neha
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Redwood proposal — ask on multi-year pricing protection

Neha / Marissa —

Operationally we can support a 3% uplift cap for a 36-month committed term, provided we: 1) require minimum commit thresholds per quarter (to avoid extreme usage variance), and 2) add a limited cost-pass-through trigger if GPU spot/contracted rates rise above +18% quarter-over-quarter. That trigger would give us the right to renegotiate uplift only under defined macro cost events.

Impact: worst-case revenue yield falls ~5% over three years at current utilization forecasts (see quick scenarios). If legal is comfortable with a defined pass-through and we get exec approval for the exception, I can bake this into the deal desk pricing model and update the quote.

Attachment: pricing-scenarios-3yr.xlsx

Ben
VP, Global Sales Operations

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 13:15:00 -0800
Subject: Exec memo for CFO/GC approval — need signoff by 3pm PT

Team — I drafted the exec memo below (for CFO and GC). Please review and flag edits. If you agree, I'll route to Markus and Legal for final signoff.

--- memo start ---
Request: Approve an exception to standard deal desk price-change policy for CloudBridge (Deal DB-4786). Requesting authorization to: 1) offer a 36-month price preservation (no increase to base per-token/embedding price) with a firm annual uplift cap of 3%; 2) include a renewal protection clause that requires 180 days' notice for material pricing changes; 3) include a narrowly-defined cost-pass-through clause triggered only when our contracted GPU/infra costs rise >18% QoQ.

Rationale: CloudBridge is a strategic platform customer with committed annualized usage that meets our dedicated tier thresholds. Securing a multi-year agreement reduces churn risk and enables capacity planning in US region. Deal Desk forecasts a 4–6% reduction in unit yield but a meaningful increase in committed ARR and decreased churn risk.

Recommended guardrails: minimum quarterly commit thresholds, quarterly usage review with CS, termination right for Redwood if infra costs exceed trigger for two consecutive quarters, and an annual reconciliation for overage billing.

Financial impact estimate: See attached scenarios.
--- memo end ---

If no material objections, I will escalate to CFO/GC. We need their OK by 3pm PT to keep CloudBridge on the procurement fast track.

-Neha

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec memo for CFO/GC approval — need signoff by 3pm PT

Neha / team —

Thanks for the clear memo. I reviewed with Finance and Legal. Approve the exception with the guardrails you proposed. Conditions: 1) include the minimum quarterly commit language, 2) cap pass-through to contract renegotiation only after two consecutive quarters above the 18% infra cost trigger, and 3) require automatic review clause at the 24-month mark to reassess pricing posture.

Marissa, Ben — please update the contract language and pricing workbook and send to CloudBridge legal with a cover note. Neha — loop in CS for the quarterly usage review plan and publish the internal escalation playbook.

-Markus
COO (on behalf of CFO/GC)
